Amelia entered this world as the only daughter of a large family of boys in a household desperately struggling to put food on the table.

Her mother worked as a scullery maid in the service of a wealthy Venetian family, and her father, much older than her mother, worked as a grave digger throughout her childhood but did not survive past her 11th year, leaving her mother with six young mouths to feed.

As the only girl in her family with five brothers, she became the constant life support for them all, physically, emotionally, spiritually, a leading heart, continuing the same cycle of servitude she observed and absorbed from her distant, exhausted, and emotionally unavailable mother, who spent much of her life in the servitude of men.
Amelia learned how to traverse the lower class white male world from a very early age.
It was all she had ever known and she understood her place in its world.
She knew what was expected, its rules and boundaries.

She had an innate strength and curiosity that equipped her with tools of awareness, listening and impulsiveness and learned how to wield her charm and wit and physical body to gain pockets of freedom.
Acutely attuned to the needs of others, she became adept at nurturing, supporting, and gratifying others in exchange for small opportunities that allowed her more agency and power.
It was an exhausting and necessary exchange, but something she eventually excelled at.
Her relationship with her brothers was complex.
There was love, certainly, but something she could not name or fully understand that complicated her relationships with men.
She had the ability to anticipate their every need and took on the role of second mother and nurturer as her own was perpetually unavailable.
She learned from them, through them, and despite their ever-changing expectations and moods, which could run the gamut of tenderness, violence, and indifference.
The lines between nurture and exclusion were frequently blurred And the eventual initiation into her own sensual, sexual self collided with theirs in tender, shameful, and ultimately confusing ways.
She learned from them as well how to defend herself and fight when she needed to.
She could be scrappy as a hellcat when necessary and supple and yielding when the situation called for that.
